plans.note: No liability or limitation heading appears in the outline; this site development and hosting agreement appears to omit a cap. Scan the general body (sec-p0001) and any boilerplate near the signature block (sec-p0072) before concluding absence, then propose a mutual cap with carve-outs.

No indemnity section surfaced. Expect to add a vendor-side indemnity for third-party IP claims arising from the hosted site and HDI's misconduct; check sec-1.4 (access/content rights) for any embedded risk allocation.

No restrictive-covenant heading visible. Because HDI is both host and an affiliated direct marketer, review sec-1.4 and the general body for any limit on the Company's ability to sell Deerskin Products through other channels.

Hosting arrangements of this type often make HDI the sole site developer/host. Check sec-1.4 (HDI's provision of access) and the general body for any sole-source or 'exclusive provider' language binding us.
No pricing or MFN heading in the outline. If any most-favoured-terms language appears in the fee provisions, confirm direction runs in our favour rather than obliging us to give HDI best terms.

No non-solicit heading appears. Sec-5.4 (each party appoints a representative) is the only personnel-related section; check it and the general body for any hiring restriction on us, and require a general-advertising carve-out if found.

The defined term 'Termination Date' shows termination mechanics exist in the body even though no heading surfaced; locate them in sec-p0001 and confirm we may exit on notice without penalty while HDI cannot walk away mid-term.

No term/renewal heading in the outline, but 'Termination Date' implies a term clause in the body; check for auto-renewal and, if present, secure a short non-renewal notice window and capped renewal pricing.

Governing law is standard boilerplate that typically sits just before the signature block; review the general body and the text preceding sec-p0072. Confirm New York, Delaware, California or England and Wales with courts rather than foreign arbitration.
Assignment is usually in the closing boilerplate near sec-p0072. Confirm we may assign to affiliates and successors and that HDI has no termination right on our change of control.

Sec-1.4 governs HDI's provision of access and is the most likely home for rights in the site and our content; 'Deerskin Products' suggests our marks and catalogue data are in scope. Confirm we own the site deliverables and all Company data, with no assignment to HDI.

Sec-1.4 is the access/grant provision. Check that any licence to us extends to our affiliates and contractors and is not revocable at HDI's discretion, and that any licence we give HDI in our marks and content is limited to operating the site.
No audit or records heading appears. If audit rights against us exist in the fee or reporting provisions, limit them to annual, notice-based, off-site review at HDI's cost.

No liquidated damages or service level heading in the outline. Check the fee and termination provisions for penalties or early-termination charges payable by us; service credits running to us are acceptable.

No warranty or service level heading surfaced. Look in the body and around sec-1.4 for HDI performance commitments on site availability; if none, propose a performance warranty with a repair-or-refund remedy.

No insurance provision appears. HDI hosts our site and handles Company and customer data, so add standard commercial, cyber and errors-and-omissions coverage with us as additional insured where appropriate.

No fee schedule or commitment heading in the outline. Review the compensation provisions in the body for minimum spend, guaranteed volumes or take-or-pay hosting fees, and pair any commitment with an exit right.

'Termination Date' confirms termination mechanics exist, but no transition or wind-down heading appears. Add return of Company data (including customer and order data) in usable format plus reasonable migration assistance after the Termination Date.
